topics.summary: This workbook applies to the supplied local teaching service. It uses private directories, loopback connections, and the included client. It is not a runbook for an employer’s infrastructure or an instruction to expose the application on a public network. Adaptation to production requires security, retention, availability, and recovery decisions that the lab intentionally does not make.

topics.title: A.6 Diagnose Pending Jobs Without Erasing Evidence
topics.summary: If a job remains pending, verify the worker endpoint and whether the worker can answer its own PING. Inspect gateway dispatch error counters as transient evidence, remembering that they reset after gateway restart. Check whether the worker receipt already exists through the supported application behavior or a controlled read-only database inspection in the private lab.

topics.title: A.8 Perform a Controlled Restart
topics.summary: Stop the gateway through its normal termination signal, retaining the database. Restart it with the same state file and the intended worker port. Verify a previously completed key, a pending key if present, and an identical duplicate. Repeat the corresponding worker restart exercise with its retained receipt file.

blocks.text: Avoid a force kill as the first ordinary shutdown method. The service has a cooperative drain path, and using it provides clearer ownership behavior. Forceful termination remains a useful controlled fault test, but it tests a different recovery history and should be recorded as such.

blocks.text: A process restart does not require deleting databases. Recreating empty state can make startup easier while losing the very evidence needed to recognize retries. Treat state removal as destructive, not as a standard troubleshooting step.

Verify a previously completed key, a pending key if present, and an identical duplicate. Repeat the corresponding worker restart exercise with its retained receipt file.

Avoid a force kill as the first ordinary shutdown method. The service has a cooperative drain path, and using it provides clearer ownership behavior. Forceful termination remains a useful controlled fault test, but it tests a different recovery history and should be recorded as such.

A process restart does not require deleting databases. Recreating empty state can make startup easier while losing the very evidence needed to recognize retries. Treat state removal as destructive, not as a standard troubleshooting step.

The integration suite manages exact process identities and cleanup. In manual work, prefer the terminal’s normal interrupt or a verified process ID over broad name-based termination commands that could affect unrelated work.
